question: What does git commit do?
options: Records the staged changes as a new snapshot in the local repository
Uploads your latest changes to the shared repository on GitHub
Downloads new changes from the remote and merges them
Marks the changed files so they are included in the next push
explanation: A commit is local. git push uploads commits, git pull downloads and merges, and git add stages files for the next commit.
source: Lecture 2, slide 5; Pro Git book p. 28

question: You run these commands. Which branch are you on afterwards?
code:
git switch main
git switch -c feature
git switch main
git merge feature
explanation: git switch -c creates and switches to feature, the third command switches back to main, and git merge doesn't change the current branch.

question: Two people changed the same line of a file on different branches. What happens when one branch is merged into the other?
options: Git stops with a merge conflict that someone has to resolve
Git keeps the change from the branch that was committed last
Git keeps both lines, one after the other, and commits
Git refuses to merge until one of the branches is deleted
explanation: Git can't know which change is right, so it marks the conflict in the file and waits for you to fix it and commit.
source: Lecture 2, slide 11; Pro Git book pp. 75–77

question: What is the main reason to keep a .gitignore file in a project?
options: To stop files like build output or secrets from being committed
To list the people who are not allowed to push to the repository
To make Git skip files when other people clone the repository
To hide the commit history of selected files
explanation: .gitignore lists untracked files Git should leave alone. Access control is set on the hosting service, and files that were committed earlier still show up in clones and history.
source: Assignment 1 p. 2; Pro Git book p. 32
